In [[mathematics]], more specifically in [[general topology]], the '''Tychonoff cube''' is the generalization of the [[unit cube]] from the [[product topology|product]] of a finite number of [[unit interval]]s to the product of an infinite, even [[uncountable set|uncountable]] number of unit intervals. The Tychonoff cube is named after [[Andrey Tychonoff]], who first considered the arbitrary product of [[topological space]]s and who proved in the 1930s that the Tychonoff cube is [[compact space|compact]]. Tychonoff later generalized this to the product of collections of arbitrary compact spaces. This result is now known as [[Tychonoff's theorem]] and is considered one of the most important results in general topology.<ref>{{Citation |last=Willard |first=Stephen |title=General Topology |location=Mineola, NY |publisher=Dover Publications |year=2004 |isbn=0-486-43479-6 }}</ref>

== Definition ==
Let <math> I </math> denote the [[unit interval]] <math>[0,1]</math>. Given a [[cardinal number]] <math>\kappa \geq \aleph_0</math>, we define a Tychonoff cube of [[Base (topology)#Weight and character|weight]] <math>\kappa</math> as the space <math> I^\kappa</math> with the [[product topology]], i.e. the product <math> \prod_{s\in S} I_s </math> where <math>\kappa </math> is the [[cardinality]] of <math> S </math> and, for all <math> s\in S </math>, <math> I_s = I </math>. 

The [[Hilbert cube]], <math> I^{\aleph_0} </math>, is a special case of a Tychonoff cube.

== Properties ==
The [[axiom of choice]] is assumed throughout.

* The Tychonoff cube is compact.
* Given a [[cardinal number]] <math>\lambda \leq \kappa</math>, the space <math> I^\lambda </math> is [[Embedding|embeddable]] in <math> I^\kappa</math>.
* The Tychonoff cube <math> I^\kappa</math> is a [[universal space]] for every [[compact space]] of [[Base (topology)#Weight and character|weight]] <math>\kappa \geq \aleph_0</math>.
* The Tychonoff cube <math> I^\kappa</math> is a [[universal space]] for every [[Tychonoff space]] of [[Base (topology)#Weight and character|weight]] <math>\kappa \geq \aleph_0</math>.
* The [[Character (topology)|character]] of <math> x\in I^\kappa </math> is <math>\kappa</math>.
* All [[Tychonoff spaces]] are [[homeomorphic]] to a subspace of a Tychonoff cube (known as the Embedding Theorem in some texts).

== See also ==
* [[Tychonoff plank]] – the [[topological product]] of the two [[ordinal space]]s <math>[0,\omega_1]</math> and <math>[0,\omega]</math>, where <math>\omega</math> is the [[first infinite ordinal]] and <math>\omega_1</math> the [[first uncountable ordinal]]
* [[Long line (topology)]] – a generalization of the [[real line]] from a countable number of line segments <nowiki>[</nowiki>0, 1) laid end-to-end to an uncountable number of such segments.
* [[Maharam's theorem]] - a statement that [[complete measure space]]s can be decomposed into unit intervals and discrete parts.
